display.title: Episode 493: The Hidden Treasure (Elul)
display.summary_short: Mid-Elul 5751, back from summer vacation: a girl's tzedakah and a fallen apple tree, Shema with a Beis Yaakov class, and a listener's composition about honoring parents.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi welcomes listeners back from summer vacation: just as we rested to strengthen the body, we strengthened the neshamah with daily davening, Torah study and tzedakah. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a third-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time, 'Reward for Kindness', begins with the teaching that the Geulah will come in the merit of tzedakah. Sarah, the daughter of a hard-working poor man, gives away her pennies and the apples from the tree behind her house to hungry families, teaching them the brachah. One stormy night the tree is blown down. Her father reminds her that whatever Hashem does is good, and when Sarah goes out to gather the last apples they find a hidden treasure in the hole left by the roots. In the mailbox, a nine-year-old girl's composition tells how she babysat so her mother could shop and her father could keep learning. The show ends with a call to enroll in a yeshiva for the new year and Shabbos candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah gladly, even when you have little; whatever Hashem does is for the good, and He repays kindness many times over.
